To: Executive Leadership Team
From: Supply Chain Director
Date: [Insert date]
Subject: Network shipping plan to meet demand at the lowest total transportation cost (whole-unit shipments)

Situation
We operate a multi-site supply network with several warehouses and factories supplying a broad set of stores and customer locations. Transportation spend is a major component of our cost to serve, and service levels depend on getting product to the right place at the right time. With varying route costs and finite inventory at each source, a focused allocation plan is required to control spend and protect customer satisfaction.

Problem
We need to determine how much to ship from each source to each destination so that:
- We do not draw more than the available inventory at any source
- Every destination receives the quantity it requires
- Shipments move at the lowest total cost across the network
- All moves are planned in whole units only (no partial loads)

Shipping costs differ by route, and some destinations may be most economically served from multiple sources. Conversely, certain lanes may be high cost and should be avoided unless necessary. The core challenge is to balance supply availability, destination needs, and lane economics while honoring whole-unit shipping requirements.

Plan
Using the latest supply availability, destination demand, and per-lane transportation costs (see Annex), we will produce a lane-level shipping plan that:
- Allocates shipments from sources to destinations to cover every requirement without exceeding available inventory
- Chooses lower-cost routes where feasible and limits use of higher-cost lanes to only what is needed
- Plans shipments strictly in whole units, aligning with operational handling (e.g., pallet or truckload increments)
- Allows destinations to be supplied by more than one source when that reduces overall spend and improves service

Once the plan is built from the data in the Annex, we will validate it with Operations and Sales, confirm carrier capacity and timing, and release allocations to sites and partners. We will monitor execution and adjust if inventory positions or demand signals change.
